title: The Clause and the Sovereign: Aurelius Capital, Argentina, and Nine Years of Refusing the Offer
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Philadelphia and the Firm on Fifty-Seventh Street

stops.name: Philadelphia, the political science degree
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia, 'Aurelius Capital Management'); month and day set to a conventional June commencement and not documented anywhere reachable
stops.campa: He takes a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Pennsylvania and then leaves the documentary record almost entirely. No source reachable here gives his birth year, his birthplace, his parents, the law school that made him a lawyer, or the bar that admitted him. What survives of Mark Brodsky's first three decades is a single line in an encyclopedia article about a company he will not found for thirty-one years. Where he goes between the commencement and the Manhattan office, and what he does there, the record does not say.
stops.quote: Mark Brodsky graduated in Political Science at the University of Pennsylvania in 1974
suggested_refs: University of Pennsylvania commencement records, class of 1974

stops.name: Manhattan, hired at Elliott Associates
stops.date_confidence: unattested placeholder: no source gives the year Brodsky joined Elliott or the year he left. 1990 is a bare anchor between the 1974 degree and the 2005 founding and must not be read as a documented date
stops.campa: Somewhere in the years between the degree and the founding he goes to work for Paul Singer at Elliott Associates, on West Fifty-seventh Street. One source calls him a lawyer formerly employed there. Another, quoting the New York Times, calls him a former trader. Nobody says which, and nobody gives a date either way. What the firm teaches in those years is a single procedure with four moves: buy a sovereign's defaulted paper at a discount from holders who have given up on it, refuse every offer of less than face, find the clause, and go to court.
stops.quote: Mark Brodsky, a lawyer formerly employed by Elliott Associates
suggested_refs: Elliott Associates offices at 40 West 57th Street, Manhattan, before the 2020 move to West Palm Beach
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bracebridge Capital', quoting the New York Times

stops.name: Manhattan, the Peruvian precedent inside the firm
stops.date_confidence: the Peru purchase and judgment are attested to Elliott for 1996; Brodsky's presence in the office in that year is inferred from his undated employment there and is not attested
stops.campa: Elliott buys Peru's defaulted paper for eleven point four million dollars and sues for face value. The judgment comes to fifty-eight million, and the two Latin words that win it are pari passu, a clause in every sovereign bond contract providing that no creditor shall rank below another. Peru pays in full. The method now exists in a form that can be repeated: the discount purchase, the refused exchange, the clause, the injunction on the payment channel. Brodsky is inside the firm while it is assembled, though no source places him in any particular room on any particular day.
stops.quote: In 1996, Elliott bought defaulted Peruvian debt for $11.4 million. Elliott won a $58 million judgment and Peru had to repay the sum in full under the pari passu rule.
suggested_refs: Elliott Associates, L.P. v. Banco de la Nacion and the Republic of Peru, SDNY and Second Circuit, 1996-2000

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the default that makes the paper
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Argentina stops paying. The size of it is given as ninety-three billion dollars of external debt in one source and one hundred and three billion in another, with roughly eighty-two billion of that in bonds; the discrepancy sits in the record and stays there. Within weeks the paper is trading in New York at a fraction of face value, and holders who bought it to hold begin selling to buyers who intend to sue. Brodsky is still at Elliott. Aurelius Capital Management does not exist and will not for four more years.
suggested_refs: The December 2001 Argentine sovereign default, the largest in history at the time
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Manhattan, Aurelius Capital Management founded
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia, 'Aurelius Capital Management'); month and day not documented and defaulted to 01
stops.campa: He leaves Singer's firm and starts his own, with Adam Stanislavsky, in an office tower at Sixth Avenue and West Fifty-fourth Street. The name is Aurelius Capital Management: a Roman name, emperor or jurist, for a fund whose entire business will be the enforcement of promises written down. The strategy is the one he learned uptown, now run on his own book. The firm stays deliberately small, a handful of employees, no retail money, no public statements from its founder. He will still be running it twenty years later.
suggested_refs: 1330 Avenue of the Americas, Manhattan, the firm's address from founding through the 2024 filings

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the first exchange and the quarter that refuses
stops.date_confidence: the 2005 exchange is attested; the January date is inherited from paul_singer.journey.json's stop for the same event, and the two sources describing the terms do not agree (see quote_source note)
stops.campa: Argentina offers the holders of its defaulted bonds an exchange: par bonds due 2038, or discount bonds due 2033 worth a fraction of the original face, given as roughly thirty percent in one source and twenty-five to thirty-five in another. Seventy-six percent of the paper comes in, some sixty-two and a half billion dollars of it. The rest does not. Aurelius is founded in this same year, becomes a holdout by purchase rather than by refusal, and buys into the refusing quarter on the secondary market. No source establishes that it held a single Argentine bond on the day the offer was made.
suggested_refs: The 2005 Argentine debt exchange, par bonds due 2038 and discount bonds due 2033
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Foley Square, Aurelius Capital Partners v. Republic of Argentina
stops.date_confidence: the reported Second Circuit decision is 584 F.3d 120 (2d Cir. 2009); the month is not established and the underlying SDNY filing date was not retrieved, court-record sites returning 403 and 404 this session
stops.campa: The caption exists before the campaign is famous: Aurelius Capital Partners, LP v. Republic of Argentina, in the Second Circuit. This is Aurelius suing in its own name over its own paper, years before the consolidated pari passu litigation makes the holdouts a subject for newspapers. Brodsky's firm is four years old. Its counterparty is a sovereign state with almost nothing in the district that a New York court can seize. The reported citation is 584 F.3d 120, and the district filing beneath the appeal precedes it by a year or two, though its date was not retrieved.
suggested_refs: Aurelius Capital Partners, LP v. Republic of Argentina, 584 F.3d 120 (2d Cir. 2009)
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.', footnote citation

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the second exchange and the lock law
stops.date_confidence: date inherited from paul_singer.journey.json's stop for the same 2010 reopening
stops.campa: Argentina reopens the offer. More of the paper comes in and the total accepted across both exchanges passes ninety percent. The Argentine Congress has already passed a lock law forbidding the executive to offer the refusers anything better than the exchange holders took, which leaves a courtroom in Manhattan as the only forum where anything better can be got. Aurelius stays out again. So does Elliott's Cayman vehicle NML Capital, and so do Davidson Kempner and Bracebridge.
suggested_refs: Argentina's Ley Cerrojo, forbidding any improved offer to the holdout creditors

stops.name: Manhattan, Griesa reads the clause
stops.date_confidence: the ruling is attested to 2012; the precise date of 23 February is taken from paul_singer.report.md section 5, and the Wikipedia article relied on here gives only the year
stops.campa: In the Daniel Patrick Moynihan courthouse on Pearl Street, Judge Thomas P. Griesa gives the equal treatment clause the reading the holdouts have been asking for since Peru: Argentina may not pay its exchange bondholders unless it pays Aurelius and NML ratably at the same moment. The order seizes nothing. It closes the pipe: a sovereign with no attachable assets in New York can still be reached through the New York bank that moves its coupon payments. The date is the twenty-third of February, 2012.
suggested_refs: The Daniel Patrick Moynihan United States Courthouse, 500 Pearl Street, seat of the SDNY proceedings from 2009 to 2016
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Foley Square, the Second Circuit affirms
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Argentina appeals across the square to the Thurgood Marshall courthouse and loses. Aurelius is on the caption throughout, standing beside NML Capital, which is Paul Singer's Cayman vehicle, and Brodsky worked for Singer before he had a firm of his own. A sovereign state is now answering two former colleagues. The panel holds that the Republic may not discriminate among its own bondholders by paying one class and stiffing another. The pari passu clause Argentina wrote into its own indentures means what it says.
suggested_refs: The Thurgood Marshall United States Courthouse, 40 Foley Square, seat of the Second Circuit appeals
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Manhattan, the number that gets misreported
stops.date_confidence: November 2012 is attested for Griesa's order fixing the amounts; the exact day is not established in any source reachable here
stops.campa: Griesa fixes what is owed. The figure that enters the press is one point three three billion dollars, repeatedly printed as Aurelius's claim. It is the aggregate owed to the whole holdout plaintiff group, of which NML alone is separately ordered two point four billion in related proceedings. What Aurelius itself is owed, and what it paid for the paper that generated the debt, are stated in no source reachable here. Brodsky does not say, then or afterward.
suggested_refs: Griesa's November 2012 order fixing the amounts payable to the holdout plaintiff group
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'
Wikipedia, 'Aurelius Capital Management' (which misdates the underlying default to 2010)

stops.name: Foley Square, affirmed a second time
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The panel affirms again and this time explains itself in terms that have nothing to do with Argentina. New York is a commercial center because contracts made in it are enforced in it; a court that lets a foreign sovereign pay some creditors and not others is spending down the city's own franchise. Argentina had promised its bondholders, among other things, free transferability of the paper, and the court holds it to what it promised. Brodsky's business rests on that reasoning. His name appears nowhere in the opinion.
stops.quote: We believe that the interest—one widely shared in the financial community—in maintaining New York's status as one of the foremost commercial centers is advanced by requiring debtors, including foreign debtors, to pay their debts.
stops.quote_source: NML Capital, Ltd. v. Republic of Argentina, 727 F.3d 230 (2d Cir. 2013), decision of 23 August 2013, quoted at Wikipedia, 'Argentine debt restructuring', footnote 61. The primary text could not be fetched this session (law.justia.com returned 403); the citation was confirmed through CourtListener.
suggested_refs: NML Capital, Ltd. v. Republic of Argentina, 727 F.3d 230 (2d Cir. 2013)
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the government that will not pay
stops.date_confidence: the epithet is attested to a 2014 United Nations address by Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner; the month is not established and the September date is a placeholder within the attested year
stops.campa: Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner will not settle. Her government calls the holdout funds fondos buitre, vulture funds, and at the United Nations she calls them economic terrorists; Argentine law forbids her cabinet to offer them better terms than the exchange bondholders received. Aurelius and NML hold court orders the Republic will not obey and cannot obey without breaking its own statute. Neither side can move. The paper sits in New York and accrues interest.
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner on the vulture funds, address at the United Nations, 2014, as quoted in Wikipedia, 'Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner'
suggested_refs: Kirchner's United Nations addresses on the fondos buitre, 2014

stops.name: Washington, the Supreme Court closes the appeals
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 7-1 discovery ruling of 16 June 2014, Scalia writing, Ginsburg dissenting, Sotomayor not participating; the widely reported same-day denial of certiorari in the pari passu case is NOT confirmed by the article relied on here and is recorded as unverified
stops.campa: On a single June morning the Court disposes of Argentina. It declines to disturb the Second Circuit's reading of the equal treatment clause, and in a separate case, seven to one with Justice Scalia writing, it upholds a discovery order permitting NML Capital to subpoena banks anywhere in the world for information about Argentine assets. There is no court above this one, and the Republic has now been through all of them. Ginsburg dissents. Sotomayor takes no part.
suggested_refs: Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd., 573 U.S. 134 (2014)
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the money that cannot be delivered
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Argentina has the money and cannot deliver it. It wires a coupon payment to its trustee in New York; the injunction forbids the trustee to pass anything on unless Aurelius and the other holdouts are paid ratably at the same time, and so the payment sits, made and undelivered. The ratings agencies record a selective default. The government in Buenos Aires refuses the word entirely and disputes that a debtor who has paid can be said to have defaulted. The coupon stays in the trustee's account.
suggested_refs: The blocked June 2014 coupon payment held at Bank of New York Mellon under the Griesa injunction
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: The Hague, the application nobody will hear
stops.date_confidence: August 2014 attested for the filing; the day is not documented and is defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Argentina files an application against the United States at the International Court of Justice, arguing that American courts have violated its sovereign immunity by ordering it to pay creditors it never agreed to pay. The case goes nowhere and can go nowhere. The United States has not accepted the Court's compulsory jurisdiction, so the application is never entered on the General List and no proceedings follow. The papers are lodged at the Peace Palace in August and nothing further happens to them.
suggested_refs: The Peace Palace, The Hague, seat of the International Court of Justice

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the RUFO clause runs out
stops.date_confidence: the expiry is attested to December 2014; the causal link to the 2016 settlement is widely understood but is not spelled out in the source relied on here
stops.campa: The obstacle has a name: Rights Upon Future Offers, the RUFO clause in the exchange bonds. It provides that if Argentina gives the holdouts better terms than the exchange holders accepted, every exchange holder may claim the same, which would turn any settlement with Aurelius into a liability of tens of billions. At the end of December the clause expires by its own terms, and from the first of January a settlement with Aurelius is arithmetically possible for the first time in nine years. Nothing else about the day is different.
suggested_refs: The RUFO clause in the 2005 and 2010 Argentine exchange bonds, expiring 31 December 2014

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Macri wins the runoff
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Mauricio Macri wins the presidential runoff, having campaigned in part on ending the standoff and getting Argentina back into the international credit markets, which requires paying the men his predecessor called terrorists at the United Nations. Kirchner hands over on the tenth of December after litigating the protocol of the handover itself. The incoming government's first serious piece of foreign business is a negotiation with four hedge funds in a mediator's office in Manhattan, and no other state is at the table.
suggested_refs: The November 2015 Argentine presidential runoff and the transition of 10 December 2015
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, six and a half billion offered
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Argentina offers the holdout creditors six and a half billion dollars and asks the New York court to lift the injunction that has kept the Republic out of the bond markets. It is the first offer any Argentine government has made to the refusers in eleven years, and it can only be made lawful by repealing two statutes and finding a congressional majority to do it. Brodsky's answer is not on the public record, and neither is almost anything else he has said about the case.
stops.quote: Argentina offered to pay $6.5 billion to settle lawsuits on 5 February 2016, requesting that the prior ruling on its payments be lifted.
suggested_refs: The February 2016 Argentine settlement proposal to the holdout creditors
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Manhattan, Griesa lifts what Griesa built
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Griesa, who has run this case since before Aurelius held any Argentine paper, orders the injunction lifted on two conditions: Argentina must repeal the lock laws that make paying the holdouts a crime under its own law, and it must pay every holdout who has settled by the twenty-ninth of February. The order that closed the pipe in 2012 is written out of existence by the judge who wrote it, on terms he sets himself, and the conditions are addressed to a legislature four thousand miles away. Ten days remain to meet them.
suggested_refs: Griesa's conditional order of 19 February 2016 vacating the pari passu injunctions
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Manhattan, the promise not to sue
stops.date_confidence: February 2016 attested; the exact day of the undertaking is not established in any source reachable here
stops.campa: Argentina cannot pay the settlements out of reserves. It has to borrow, and the men it owes are exactly the ones with standing to attach the proceeds of a new bond issue. So Aurelius, Davidson Kempner and Bracebridge give the undertaking that makes the whole arrangement executable: they will not try to stop the Republic raising the money with which the Republic will pay them. It is the clearest documented instance of Brodsky acting in direct concert with Paul Singer, and what he contributes is a promise not to sue. The exact day of the undertaking is not established.
suggested_refs: Reporting on the February 2016 settlement, cited at Wikipedia, 'Bracebridge Capital'

stops.name: Manhattan, the mediator announces
stops.date_confidence: February 2016 attested for Pollack's announcement of the Singer agreement; the 29 February date is the court-imposed payment deadline and is used here as the anchor
stops.campa: Daniel Pollack, the special master appointed to mediate, announces that Argentina has reached agreement with Paul Singer. The headline settlement is Elliott's, as the headline claim always was. Aurelius settles in the same window and on comparable terms, and no figure specific to Brodsky's fund appears in any source reachable here. The reported totals give roughly four point six five three billion dollars to the four lead holdouts as a group, of which Elliott takes about two point four.
suggested_refs: Daniel Pollack's mediation of the Argentine holdout settlements, 2014-2016
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'
paul_singer.report.md, section 6, citing Financial Times figures

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Congress unwrites the law
stops.date_confidence: March 2016 attested for the congressional approval; the 31 March date is inherited from paul_singer.journey.json's stop for the same vote
stops.campa: The Argentine Congress repeals the Ley Cerrojo and the Sovereign Payment Law, the two statutes that made paying Aurelius a crime under Argentine law, and authorizes the borrowing that will fund the settlements. That vote is the substantive concession; everything after it is mechanics and wire instructions. A legislature in Buenos Aires has to unwrite its own law before a New York fund can be paid on bonds it bought at a discount from people who had already written the money off. No Argentine government had been able to assemble the votes for eleven years.
suggested_refs: The March 2016 repeal of the Ley Cerrojo and the Sovereign Payment Law

stops.name: Foley Square, affirmed from the bench
stops.date_confidence: attested; a duplicate entry in the research pool dating a second court confirmation to 14 April 2016 was rejected, 14 April being the expiry of the settlement offer's stated validity rather than a separate ruling
stops.campa: The New York court confirms Griesa's ruling and clears the Republic to pay the 2005 exchange holders, the 2010 exchange holders, and the holdouts alike, which is the first time in the case that all three classes appear in one sentence as people who will be paid. The deal's own terms give it validity only through the fourteenth, one day away. The Second Circuit affirms from the bench, without retiring to write the opinion first, and the argument is over by the afternoon.
suggested_refs: The Second Circuit's bench affirmance of 13 April 2016
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.'

stops.name: Manhattan, Aurelius is paid
stops.date_confidence: attested; note the unexplained gap between this payment date and the 14 April expiry of the settlement offer's stated validity, which no reachable source accounts for
stops.campa: Argentina borrows on the international markets for the first time since the default and pays the holdouts out of the proceeds. The wire goes out on the twenty-second of April, eight days after the settlement offer's stated validity had expired; the sources record both dates and explain neither. The money moves through New York, which is what the entire case was about, money moving through New York. In the coverage of his own victory Brodsky is one name in a list of four. He issues no statement and gives no interview.
suggested_refs: Argentina's April 2016 international bond issue funding the holdout settlements
sources: Wikipedia, 'Fondo buitre' (Spanish), which gives a figure of US$9.3 billion paid to the vulture funds in 2016, not reconciled with the $4.653 billion reported to the four lead holdouts

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the creditors paid last
stops.date_confidence: November 2016 attested; the day is not documented and is defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Argentina reports settling with the remaining smaller holdout creditors for a further four hundred and seventy-five million dollars. These are the claims that were never going to move a market or a judge: Italian and German retail holders, pension funds, individuals who bought the bonds before the default and simply never sold. They are paid last, on terms set by the leverage of the four funds that went to court and stayed there. Whether any of them recovered what they originally paid for the bonds is not reported anywhere reachable here.
suggested_refs: The November 2016 settlements with the residual Argentine holdout creditors

stops.name: Manchester, the Co-operative Bank renegotiated
stops.date_confidence: October 2013 attested for the renegotiated rescue; the day is not documented and is defaulted to 01
stops.campa: The Co-operative Bank needs rescuing, and the rescue as first drawn would leave its parent mutual holding seventy-five percent of the recapitalized bank. Aurelius, with Beach Point Capital and Silver Point Capital, holds the subordinated debt and renegotiates. By October the Co-operative Group's stake has been cut to thirty percent and the bondholders take the remainder. The bank was founded on Balloon Street in Manchester by British cooperators. Its owners are now largely American distressed debt funds, by the arithmetic of who was holding the subordinated paper.
suggested_refs: The Co-operative Bank headquarters, Balloon Street, Manchester

stops.name: London, the High Court approves the scheme
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The High Court approves the restructuring on the eighteenth of December and the transfer is done. Aurelius's role in the negotiation is documented; what it paid for its position, and what it made on the exit, are in no source reachable here. That is the ordinary condition of the record on Brodsky's firm. The outcomes are public because courts are public, and no statement from Brodsky about this one appears anywhere reachable. The trades are private, and Aurelius files only what regulation requires of it.
suggested_refs: The High Court's approval of the Co-operative Bank recapitalization, 18 December 2013

stops.name: Kyiv, the Ukrainian position
stops.date_confidence: the date is that of the Reuters report disclosing the position, not of any purchase; the acquisition date and the eventual outcome are undocumented in anything reachable here
stops.campa: Ukraine, at war in its east and negotiating a restructuring of its sovereign debt, finds Aurelius among its bondholders. Reuters reports in September that the fund holds a position and is asking for better terms than the other creditors are being offered. It is the Argentine posture on a smaller scale, in a country with a war on. What Aurelius ultimately received is not stated in any reachable source, and neither is the date it bought in or the size of the position Reuters was told about.
suggested_refs: Rao and Spink, Reuters, 18 September 2015, 'Exclusive: Hedge fund Aurelius holds Ukraine debt, asking better terms - source'

stops.name: Manhattan, the Petrobras bonds
stops.date_confidence: undated in every reachable source: the Petrobras activity is listed among Aurelius's positions with no year, no position size and no outcome. 2016 is a bare placeholder and carries no evidentiary weight
stops.campa: Some fifty-four billion dollars of Petrobras bonds are governed by New York law, which means that a Brazilian state oil company caught in the largest corruption investigation in the hemisphere can be sued in the same buildings on Foley Square as Argentina. That choice of law was made years earlier by somebody drafting an indenture, and it is the only reason the firm is in the room at all. Aurelius pushes for treatment favorable to a distressed holder. No source reachable here gives the size of the position. None gives the result.
suggested_refs: Petrobras bonds issued under New York law and the litigation arising from the Lava Jato investigation

stops.name: Manhattan, the names with nothing attached
stops.date_confidence: undated: Dubai World and the Tribune Company bankruptcy appear in the record of Aurelius's activity with no dates, position sizes or outcomes whatsoever. The 2016 anchor is arbitrary, chosen only to keep this stop in file order after the other undated positions, and is recorded here as a gap, not a date
stops.campa: Dubai World. The Tribune Company bankruptcy. The names appear in the record of Aurelius's activity with no dates, no position sizes, and no outcomes, so a good part of the firm's own history consists of matters it was reported to be in. What Brodsky puts into these rooms is a willingness to be the last creditor who has not agreed. The firm doing it has fourteen employees and a few hundred million dollars under management, against the largest sovereign and corporate restructurings of two decades.
suggested_refs: The Dubai World restructuring and the Tribune Company bankruptcy, both listed without detail in the record of Aurelius's activity

stops.name: San Juan, four hundred and sixty-eight million of the island's paper
stops.date_confidence: the year of the position is attested; the acquisition dates are not documented, and the January anchor is a default
stops.campa: Puerto Rico carries roughly seventy-four billion dollars of bond debt and another forty-nine billion in unfunded pensions, and it is not a state and not a country, so it can neither default the way Argentina defaulted nor file the way a city files. Aurelius holds about four hundred and sixty-eight million dollars of the island's paper. The structure is one Brodsky already knows: a debtor that cannot pay, and a legal regime nobody designed for the case in front of it. When the position was bought, and at what price, is not documented.
suggested_refs: The Puerto Rican government-debt crisis and the island's general obligation bonds

stops.name: San Juan, the Title III filing
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Governor Ricardo Rossello has the federally created Oversight Board file under Title III of PROMESA, the statute Congress wrote because Puerto Rico is barred from ordinary municipal bankruptcy. It is the largest public debt restructuring in American history: one hundred and twenty-three billion in liabilities, seventy-four in bonds and forty-nine in pensions. The board, seven members appointed by the President from lists supplied by congressional leaders, none confirmed by the Senate, now decides what every creditor will be offered.
suggested_refs: PROMESA Title III proceedings, filed 3 May 2017

stops.name: San Juan, Olson files the Appointments Clause suit
stops.date_confidence: attested; a date of 2018 in the research pool was rejected, 2018 being the year the District Court for Puerto Rico denied the motion to dismiss rather than the year of filing
stops.campa: Aurelius hires Theodore Olson, a former Solicitor General of the United States, and attacks not the numbers but the board itself. Its members exercise significant authority under a federal statute, so the Appointments Clause required Senate confirmation, and they were never confirmed. If the argument wins, every order the board has made is void and the whole restructuring restarts. Brodsky's firm has again found its leverage in a sentence somebody else wrote long ago. The sentence Olson is reading was written in 1787.
stops.quote: On August 7, 2017, Aurelius Capital Management had Theodore Olson file another lawsuit, which now alleged that the selection of the Oversight Board violated the Appointments Clause of the US Constitution.
suggested_refs: Aurelius Investment, LLC's Appointments Clause challenge to the Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico
sources: Wikipedia, 'Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico v. Aurelius Investment, LLC'

stops.name: Boston, the First Circuit agrees and withholds the remedy
stops.date_confidence: February 2019 attested for the combined ruling; the exact day is not established in any source reachable here and 15 February is a placeholder within the attested month
stops.campa: The First Circuit agrees with the creditors. The board's members hold positions established by federal law, their appointments required Senate confirmation, and they were unconstitutionally appointed. The court then declines to unwind anything the board has already done and gives the President ninety days to reappoint validly. Aurelius has won the constitutional point and been refused the consequence that would have made it worth money. The board is reappointed and carries on restructuring the island's debt exactly as before.
stops.quote: In a combined ruling in February 2019, the First Circuit reversed the special court's findings and agreed with the creditors that the appointment of members to the FCB, while not to a federal position but established by a federal law, required Senate confirmation, and thus their appointments were unconstitutional.
stops.quote_source: Wikipedia, 'Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico v. Aurelius Investment, LLC' (English), fetched 2026-08-15
suggested_refs: Aurelius Inv., LLC v. Puerto Rico, 915 F.3d 838 (1st Cir. 2019)
sources: Wikipedia, 'Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico v. Aurelius Investment, LLC'

stops.name: Washington, the case argued under his firm's name
stops.date_confidence: attested; certiorari was granted 20 June 2019 and the case argued 15 October 2019
stops.campa: Certiorari is granted in June and the case is argued in October under a caption that puts the parties in their proper order: Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico v. Aurelius Investment, LLC. A hedge fund holding four hundred and sixty-eight million dollars of a territory's bonds is the named respondent in a separation of powers case about how the United States governs three million of its own citizens. Whether Brodsky sat in the courtroom that morning is not recorded anywhere reachable.
suggested_refs: Oral argument in Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico v. Aurelius Investment, LLC, 15 October 2019
sources: Wikipedia, 'Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico v. Aurelius Investment, LLC'

stops.name: San Juan, the thirty-five billion in general obligations
stops.date_confidence: February 2020 attested; the day is not documented and is defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Court-ordered mediation produces a revised restructuring covering thirty-five billion dollars of general obligation bonds, with improved recoveries for the holders and a resolution of the long argument over whether the island's borrowing after 2012 was validly issued at all. Aurelius is among the creditors it covers. The deal does not depend on the constitutional question still pending in Washington. It is announced in February; the Court rules in June.
suggested_refs: The February 2020 mediated Puerto Rico general obligation restructuring agreement

stops.name: Washington, Breyer writes and Brodsky loses
stops.date_confidence: attested; note that the judgment is unanimous but the reasoning is not, Thomas and Sotomayor each concurring only in the judgment, so the ruling should not be described as a unanimous opinion
stops.campa: The Court rules against Aurelius. Justice Breyer writes that the Appointments Clause reaches Officers of the United States, and that these board members, though the board was created by federal statute, exercise primarily local powers within Puerto Rico and are therefore not federal officers at all. Thomas concurs while rejecting the majority's account of the board's duties as primarily local. Sotomayor concurs while attacking the arrangement itself, in terms that have nothing to do with bonds. The judgment is unanimous; the reasoning is not.
stops.quote: this freewheeling exercise of control over a population
stops.quote_source: Justice Sonia Sotomayor, concurring in the judgment, Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico v. Aurelius Investment, LLC, 1 June 2020

stops.name: Manhattan, the word that follows the firm
stops.date_confidence: undated: the epithet attaches across the whole Argentine campaign rather than to any one day, and the June 2014 anchor is placed at the height of the litigation for want of a documented date
stops.campa: The word is vulture, buitre in Spanish, and it means a creditor who buys the paper of the dying at a discount and then waits. Aurelius carries it exactly as Elliott carries it. The encyclopedia sentence applying the word to Aurelius over Argentine debt hangs on a Reuters article about Ukrainian debt that never uses it of Argentina and never offers it as Reuters's own characterization. The epithet is real and everywhere in the Argentine press. That particular citation for it does not hold.
suggested_refs: Rao and Spink, Reuters, 18 September 2015, the footnote carrying the 'vultures' characterization at Wikipedia, 'Aurelius Capital Management'

stops.name: Manhattan, the filing of May 2024
stops.date_confidence: attested, being the date of the filing cited
stops.campa: A regulatory filing dated the twenty-ninth of May puts Aurelius Capital Management at roughly eight hundred and thirty-one million dollars under management with fourteen employees, still at 1330 Avenue of the Americas, still run by Mark Brodsky. There is no encyclopedia article about him. Everything recorded is folded into the entry for the company: one degree, one former employer, one co-founder, and the case names. He beat a sovereign state in the courts of the United States and wrote no memoir about it. No interview with him, and no photograph of him, was found anywhere reachable here.
suggested_refs: Aurelius Capital Management regulatory filing dated 29 May 2024
